page: Amazon Web Services a1.large is a general-purpose cloud instance built on first-generation AWS Graviton processors. Powered by the arm64 architecture, this instance features 2 dedicated physical cores using ARMv8 Cortex-A72 microarchitecture running at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. It is provisioned with 4.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), featuring 32 KB of L1 instruction cache per core and 2 MB of shared L2 cache. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it provides a dedicated CPU allocation without multi-threading. The instance includes hardware support for AES encryption, features a 1 Gbps baseline network throughput, and contains no local NVMe storage, relying entirely on remote EBS volumes.

Performance benchmarks reflect the early-generation ARM architecture profile. The instance achieves an average single-core CPU stress-ng score of 1489.88, but falls into lower performance tiers for multi-core scaling with a stress-ng multi-core result of 2934.26. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 406.0 and a multi-core score of 700.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 785.09. Memory bandwidth performance registers at 11.18 GB/sec for large block reads and 6.69 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific throughput metrics record 0.91 million operations per second in Redis SET tasks, 0.61 GB/sec in static web serving, and 5.35 tokens per second for small 135M parameter LLM text generation.

The a1.large server offers qualitative cost efficiency for organizations looking to deploy or test applications natively compiled for 64-bit ARM architectures. Due to its lower single-thread and memory bandwidth metrics compared to newer x86 or Graviton generations, it presents tradeoffs in heavy compute, high-concurrency database, or large-scale data processing roles. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, microservices, containerized ARM build environments, and developer testing.
description: Amazon Web Services a1.large is an arm64 general-purpose server powered by first-generation AWS Graviton ARMv8 Cortex-A72 processors. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it offers 2 dedicated physical vCPUs running at 2.3 GHz, 4.0 GB of RAM, and a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. The server lacks local NVMe storage and relies entirely on network-attached storage. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate moderate single-core capabilities with a stress-ng single-core score of 1489.88, though memory bandwidth and multi-core scores remain low across standard evaluations. Hardware-accelerated AES instructions are supported natively. Given its ARM hardware profile, the instance provides qualitative cost efficiencies for ARM-native development, light web microservices, and containerized testing workloads that do not demand high memory bandwidth or intensive parallel processing capabilities.
